title: Sorted Arrays Median
statement:
Find the median of all values held in two sorted arrays without merging them.

Contract
- `first` and `second` are non-null and each is sorted ascending (duplicates allowed). Either may be empty, but not both: if both are empty, throw `IllegalArgumentException`.
- The median is the middle value of all `first.length + second.length` values in sorted order; with an even count it is the average of the two middle values.
- Return it as a `double`. Add values with `long` arithmetic so extreme `int` values cannot overflow, and keep the `.5` of an even-count average.
- Do not mutate either array. The intended solution runs in logarithmic time in the length of the shorter array.

Examples
- `median(new int[]{1, 3}, new int[]{2})` returns `2.0`.
- `median(new int[]{1, 2}, new int[]{3, 4})` returns `2.5`.
- `median(new int[]{}, new int[]{5})` returns `5.0`.
hints: Merging both arrays and picking the middle works but costs time linear in both lengths. Ask which values would land on the left half of the merged order.

Choose how many values `i` of the shorter array go to the left half; the longer array then supplies exactly `half - i` of them. The split is right when every value on the left is at most every value on the right.

Binary search `i` on the shorter array, comparing the four border values and treating missing borders as minus or plus infinity. Odd total: the answer is the larger left border; even total: average it with the smaller right border. Intended complexity: O(log min(m, n)) time and O(1) extra space for arrays of lengths m and n.
inputSyntax: Input: the first sorted array, then the second, for example: [1, 3] [2]
